# How can I take a break from my business without losing customers? | The Automate Stack

## The short answer

Let the basics run without you. Automatic replies, link delivery, payment confirmation and lead capture can keep going while you rest. Decide in advance what must be answered fast, what can wait and what only you can handle. Then a weekend away stops costing you sales, and your phone stops owning you.

It is Saturday. You want to switch off your phone.

But you do not. Because if you do not reply in the next hour, someone might buy from someone else.

So you keep checking. You are technically resting and mentally at work. That is not a break.

Three steps: replies and links run on their own, orders and leads are captured, you return to a clear summary.

## The real fear

You are not afraid of missing a message. You are afraid of missing a sale. Fair.

So solve that, not the phone habit. If the sale does not depend on you being there, the phone can stay in the drawer.

## What can run without you

Four things matter most. A quick first reply to common questions. Delivery of the link or the product after payment. Capturing the buyer's details so you can follow up. And a note that sets expectations for anything else.

Say a buyer messages on Sunday asking about price and how to order. The reply answers both and sends the checkout link. If they pay, the confirmation goes out. You see it on Monday.

## Decide what is urgent

Not everything can wait. Complaints, large orders and special requests may need you. Set a rule, and let the system tag those so you see them first.

[Here is how I think about night replies](https://www.theautomatestack.com/blog/how-do-i-reply-to-instagram-dms-at-night-without-staying-awake/), which works for weekends too.

## The steps

1.  **List what costs you sales when you are away.** Usually replies and links.
2.  **Automate those first.** Reply, link, confirmation.
3.  **Set an urgent rule.** What should reach you at once.
4.  **Add an away message.** When you will respond.
5.  **Do a one-day trial.** Before a long break.
6.  **Return to a summary.** One list of what happened.

A business that cannot survive a weekend is not yet a business. It is a job you cannot leave.

## Questions people ask

### What if someone needs me urgently?

Set a rule for what counts as urgent and have the system flag it to you, or to someone you trust.

### Should I tell customers I am away?

Yes. A short note about when you will reply keeps trust high.

## Keep reading

-   ### [How do I stop answering the same customer questions twenty times a day?](https://www.theautomatestack.com/blog/how-do-i-stop-answering-the-same-customer-questions-twenty-times-a-day/)

    Write the answers once, then put them where customers ask. Turn your top ten questions into saved replies, a short FAQ page and an automatic first response that handles price, delivery, payment and order status. You still step in for anything unusual, but the repeats stop eating your day.

-   ### [Why do people ask for my price in the DMs and never reply again?](https://www.theautomatestack.com/blog/why-do-people-ask-for-my-price-in-the-dms-and-never-reply-again/)

    Because by the time you answered, they had already moved on. A price question is a buying signal with a short shelf life. If the reply comes hours later, the buyer has asked someone else. An automatic first reply that gives the price or a link and asks one question keeps the conversation alive while you are busy.

-   ### [Why does my Instagram DM bot break when customers make typos?](https://www.theautomatestack.com/blog/why-does-my-instagram-dm-bot-break-when-customers-make-typos/)

    Most DM bots look for one exact word. If the customer writes it differently, the bot finds no match and goes silent or repeats a menu. The fix is a setup that reads the whole message, so a typo, slang or a normal sentence still gets the right answer.
